markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 9.7% sampled negative-wins rate, versus 1.32% for CDs_and_Vinyl. This motivates category-specific analysis, but does not establish validation ranking quality. (2) Embedding scores near 0.5 indicate approximately zero mean cosine similarity. They provide little justification for collapse-focused regularization. (3) Qualitative feedback suggests excessive influence from older interests. Prefix removal tests this hypothesis without assuming ownership, compatibility requirements, or purchase readiness.

**Related work.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* separates recency effects from order sensitivity [1]. Preserving a recent suffix makes that distinction experimentally useful. (2) Recency sampling changes training-target exposure [2]. Consequently, cropping requires a control with identical supervised targets. (3) Sampled metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings [3]. Training margins therefore remain diagnostic, while the fixed host validation HR@10 determines selection.

### Directions and framework

Organize experiments around three directions: context intervention, supervision control, and ranking measurement.

| Condition | Recurrent context | Supervised positions |
|---|---|---|
| A: baseline | Full | All valid |
| B: matched control | Full | Retained suffix |
| C: prefix removal | Retained suffix | Same as B |

C−B measures the effect of removing context under matched supervision; B−A measures the supervision-policy effect. Neither comparison establishes a mechanism beyond this intervention.

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched prefix removal: 5/8/3.** Originality: useful controlled combination, although cropping is established. Potential: reusable context experiment, although benefits remain unmeasured. Difficulty: small sampler/mask change, although recurrent padding needs care [1,2].
- **Old-prefix shuffling: 4/6/3.** Originality: isolates older order, although closely follows existing perturbation work. Potential: distinguishes order from recency, although shuffled histories may be unrealistic. Difficulty: straightforward permutation, although matched supervision requires discipline [1].
- **Jointly learned recurrent decay: 5/7/6.** Originality: incorporates recency into one GRU, although decay gates are established. Potential: adapts context retention, although sparse histories may poorly identify decay. Difficulty: compact parameterization, although architecture and predictor changes increase debugging cost.

### Selected idea: matched prefix removal

At 20% progress, prioritize the first idea: it preserves the corrected GRU4Rec architecture and directly tests the existing hypothesis.

```python
sequence, positive, negative = sample_batch(...)
keep = draw_suffix_mask(sequence, dedicated_rng)
context = sequence if condition != 'C' else sequence * keep
supervise = valid if condition == 'A' else valid & keep
features = model.log2feats(context)
loss = baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, supervise)
```

Generate identical base batches, negatives, and crop masks for B/C. Normalize their losses identically; keep updates, seeds, and hyperparameters fixed. Skip padded recurrent updates and read the final nonpadding position. Inference uses full supplied histories.

Train conditions separately within budget; select one condition by macro validation HR@10 and retain one checkpoint per category. Preserve routing, predictor consistency, and diagnostic interfaces. Report paired hit/miss changes where host outputs permit; user bootstrap uncertainty excludes training-seed uncertainty. No improvement is claimed before evaluation.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic old-prefix removal in corrected GRU4Rec through three separate conditions: unchanged baseline, full-context training with suffix-only supervision, and cropped-context training with identical suffix supervision. Select one condition using macro validation HR@10 and deploy exactly one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests older interactions may distract from recent interests, but sampled training margins cannot establish that mechanism. Matching retained targets isolates context removal from changes in the supervision policy.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied corrected GRU4Rec, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four categories, splits, evaluator, and DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Use a dedicated crop RNG so mask generation does not perturb base sampling or dropout streams. Match initial parameters, base batches, negative candidates, supervised positions, and loss normalization between the matched control and cropped condition. Sample a contiguous suffix of valid input positions, retaining the last valid position; leave one-position histories unchanged. Keep aligned positive/negative targets at their original positions. Padding must not update recurrent state. Preserve log2feats, item_emb, predict_score, ModelView, DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt. Verify the embedded predictor matches the saved architecture and uses final-nonpadding readout. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Run conditions as separate experiments only as the shared budget allows; never fuse their predictions or checkpoints. Unsupported metadata and simulator traits remain unavailable.
idea.pseudocode:
For each predefined condition A, B, C:
  For each of the four categories:
    initialize the corrected GRU4Rec with training seed 42
    initialize a separate deterministic crop generator
    for each permitted training update:
      _, sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
      valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0) & (negative != 0)
      keep = sample_contiguous_suffix_of_nonpadding(sequence, crop_generator)
      input_sequence = sequence * keep if condition == C else sequence
      supervision = valid if condition == A else valid & keep
      features = model.log2feats(input_sequence)
      loss = supplied_loss(features, positive, negative, supervision)
      update this model only
    save one model checkpoint and its consistent predictor artifacts
  obtain fixed host macro validation HR@10
Select one condition by macro validation HR@10.
Deploy its four category checkpoints, loading exactly one model for each category.
Retain diagnostic metrics and definitions; interpret context effects as hypotheses until supported by measured comparisons.

originality.positive: Combines a simple GRU context intervention with a matched-target control that makes its effect easier to interpret.
originality.negative: Prefix cropping and recency-focused training are established techniques; the contribution is experimental isolation rather than a new backbone.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable test of whether context retention or supervision allocation should guide subsequent single-model improvements.
future_potential.negative: No validation improvement has been demonstrated, and results from one training seed cannot establish robustness across training randomness.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily requires an input mask and a supervision mask while preserving the existing architecture and predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding behavior, synchronized sampling, and equal loss normalization require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Uses interaction-order perturbations to investigate sequential recommendation benchmarks.
Motivates separating order sensitivity from the influence of recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish that stochastic prefix removal improves this corrected GRU4Rec on the four supplied datasets.
Perturbation sensitivity alone cannot identify useful historical context.

related_work.title: Recency sampling for sequential recommendation
contributions: Motivates treating target exposure as a separate experimental variable.
limitations: Changing sampled targets differs from removing context while holding supervised targets fixed.
Its findings do not supply measured results for the proposed three-condition experiment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Supports distinguishing sampled training diagnostics from the fixed benchmark selection metric.
limitations: Does not determine which proposed training condition will perform best.
Does not justify changing the host's pinned candidate sampling or evaluator.
